title: A claim names its holder, and a second holder's claim is refused

story.i_want_to: have loopctl refuse every other session that reaches for my item, even one with my agent_id
story.so_that: two sessions on one fleet never work, release or report the same item (loopctl#707)

rationale: A claim records only stories.assigned_agent_id (lib/loopctl/progress.ex:311), and every claimant check compares agent ids: start and request-review through validate_assigned_agent/2 (:5001), renew through validate_claimant/2 (:2723-2725), unclaim through validate_unclaim/2 (:5230). Every fleet session shares one agent, so any of them passes for any other. Channel claims have the same hole: a peer session's claim on a held ref returns {:ok, existing, :already_held} because it matches on claimant_agent_id (lib/loopctl/coordination.ex:2393-2399), KB finding 0264d7e0. PRD R3: a claim on a held item by any other holder is refused, whatever agent_id both share.

acceptance_criteria.description: stories gains a nullable assigned_holder_id (FK holders, never cast); Progress.claim_story/3 and BulkOperations.bulk_claim/4 write it from the caller's server-resolved holder (opts :holder_id, set only by the controller from the authenticating key), and every claim release clears it through Progress.claim_release_change/1 and release_claim_changes/1.

A claim on a story that holder H already holds at the current claim_epoch, made by H again, returns {:ok, story} with the epoch and lease unchanged and no new audit row, so a retried claim whose response was lost is not a second claim.

A claim on a story in assigned or implementing whose assigned_holder_id is H, by any caller that is not H (another holder of the same agent, or a key with no holder), returns {:error, {:held_by_other_holder, H}}, rendered 409 code held_by_other_holder with holder_id, holder kind and host.

On a story whose assigned_holder_id is H, start, renew_claim, request_review and unclaim refuse every caller that is not H with the same {:held_by_other_holder, H}, even when the caller's agent_id equals assigned_agent_id; on a story with no assigned_holder_id (claimed before this release) they keep today's agent-id checks.

Two holders of one agent claiming the same contracted story at once yield one {:ok, story} and one {:error, {:held_by_other_holder, winner}}: the loser's re-read under the story lock (lock_story/2) sees the winner's holder.

channel_claims gains claimant_holder_id, stamped server-side from the caller's holder; resolve_claim_collision/4 answers {:ok, existing, :already_held} only when the existing claim's claimant_holder_id equals the caller's (or both are nil and the agent matches), and {:error, :already_claimed} when a different holder of the same agent holds it live.

Channel claim done and release by a caller whose holder differs from a non-nil claimant_holder_id answer {:error, :not_found} (the owner-scoped fetch adds the holder), whatever claimed_by_session the caller sends.

The MCP tools claim_story, start_story, renew_story_claim, request_review, channel_claim, channel_done and channel_release say in their descriptions that a story or ref held by another session is refused 409 held_by_other_holder (stories) or already_claimed (channel), naming the holder.

test_cases.name: claim writes the holder; the same holder's retry is idempotent; release clears it (DataCase)
preconditions: contracted story; holders H1 of agent A (provided by US-52.13)
steps: Progress.claim_story(tenant, story, agent_id: a, holder_id: h1)
Progress.unclaim_story(tenant, story, agent_id: a, holder_id: h1)
expected_results: assigned_holder_id = h1; second call same claim_epoch and one status_changed audit row; after unclaim assigned_holder_id nil

test_cases.name: a second holder of the same agent is refused on every claimant verb (DataCase)
preconditions: story claimed by H1; holder H2 of the same agent; a plain key of the same agent
steps: claim, start, renew_claim, request_review, unclaim as H2
expected_results: each H2 and plain-key call {:error, {:held_by_other_holder, h1}}; H1 start succeeds

test_cases.name: a pre-release claim with no holder keeps agent-id checks (DataCase)
preconditions: story assigned with assigned_agent_id a and assigned_holder_id nil
steps: start as a plain key of agent a
start as a key of agent b

test_cases.name: two holders race one claim (DataCase, committed, ProductionTopology)
preconditions: contracted story; holders H1, H2 of one agent; async: false with the reason in the moduledoc (committed transactions racing)
expected_results: exactly one {:ok, _}; the other names the winner

test_cases.name: 409 body and the role gate (ConnCase)
preconditions: story held by H1; credentials of H1 and H2; an orchestrator key
steps: the same with the orchestrator key

test_cases.name: channel claims split by holder (DataCase)
preconditions: project; holders H1, H2 of agent A; tenant B with its own project
steps: Coordination.claim as H1 on ref r
done as H2 with H1's claimed_by_session
claim on ref r in tenant B as a tenant-B holder

test_cases.name: tool descriptions name the refusal
steps: read the seven descriptions in node --test
expected_results: each names held_by_other_holder or already_claimed and 'another session'

technical_notes: Claim: do_claim_story/3 (lib/loopctl/progress.ex:283) locks with lock_story/2 (:4947) then validate_transition_ctx/3 (:294, :4982); put the holder check BEFORE the transition check, so a held story answers held_by_other_holder rather than invalid_transition, and the same-holder idempotent return before both.

Claimant checks to change: validate_assigned_agent/2 (:5001, callers :1203 start, :1543 request_review, :1746 review_request_lost), validate_claimant/2 (:2723-2725, renew_claim :2212), validate_unclaim/2 (:5230), mark_review_requested/2's conditional UPDATE (:1718) gains assigned_holder_id. One private helper validate_holder/3 decides holder-vs-agent for all of them.

Release paths that must clear assigned_holder_id: claim_release_change/1 (:2041), release_claim_changes/1 (:2140), force_unclaim_story/3 (:4015), reclaim_expired_claim/3 (:2365), BulkOperations auto-reset (lib/loopctl/bulk_operations.ex:667-677); bulk_claim writes it at :597.

Controller: StoryStatusController.claim/2 (lib/loopctl_web/controllers/story_status_controller.ex:424) merges agent_id at :430; add holder_id: api_key.holder_id the same way for claim, start, renew_claim, request_review, unclaim. Custody identity is never a param (CLAUDE.md, Dependency Injection).

The holder on a key: api_keys.holder_id, provided by US-52.13. The 409 renders through FallbackController; add it to each route's operation/2 and CHANGELOG.md (changed behaviour of existing endpoints).

Channel: ChannelClaim schema lib/loopctl/coordination/channel_claim.ex:95-106 (claimant_holder_id set programmatically like claimant_agent_id, :25-29); claim/5 at lib/loopctl/coordination.ex:1660 takes :holder_id in opts; resolve_claim_collision/4 :2389; fetch_owned_claim/4 :2296 adds the holder predicate when non-nil. claimed_by_session stays advisory. release 7 deletes channel_claims (PRD section 4); this keeps it correct until then.
Migration: two nullable columns plus indexes on stories(assigned_holder_id) and channel_claims(claimant_holder_id); no backfill (existing claims have no holder and keep agent checks).
non_goals: Runner sessions' claims carrying a holder: US-52.15.
Holder claims following the holder's lease: US-52.19.
Report and review-complete self-gates keyed on holder: they stay lineage plus agent (CLAUDE.md, Chain-of-Custody Enforcement); verify's clause moves in US-52.15.

failure_modes.partition: AC-52.14.4: a holder cut off loses nothing it holds; no other session can start, renew or release its claim while it is away, and the lease decides when it ends.
failure_modes.state: AC-52.14.1: who holds an item is stories.assigned_holder_id under the story row lock; no client file or channel post holds it.
failure_modes.retry: AC-52.14.2: a retried claim by the same holder returns the claim unchanged; a different holder's is refused (AC-52.14.3).
failure_modes.slow: AC-52.14.5: the claim runs under lock_story/2's FOR UPDATE, so a slow second claimant waits and then reads the winner's holder.
failure_modes.reach: n/a: every check runs inline in the request process against loopctl's database; no job or remote process is involved.

defaults: A key with no holder is treated as a different holder from any holder, so a legacy LOOPCTL_AGENT_KEY cannot act on a holder's claim.
definition_of_done: Two Claude Code sessions in two worktrees of one repo on minis: the second's claim_story on the first's story returns 409 held_by_other_holder naming the first's holder and host.
